summary: Sporting News previews USC basketball ahead of Bronny James' expected collegiate debut against Long Beach State on Sunday. The Trojans are 8 games in and still lack an identity after an 89-76 loss to Gonzaga, but they have talent in Isaiah Collier, Boogie Ellis and a deep frontcourt. The piece covers futures odds, the Pac-12 race led by Arizona, the game's point spread and USC's upcoming schedule.
one_line: Ahead of Bronny James' expected debut vs. Long Beach State, USC's inconsistent 8-game start, futures odds, Pac-12 outlook and schedule are reviewed.
key_facts: USC has played eight games, roughly a quarter of its schedule, and hasn't forged an identity under coach Andy Enfield.
USC lost to Gonzaga 89-76 in Las Vegas at MGM Grand Garden Arena on Dec. 2; Gonzaga led by as many as 18 and outscored USC 21-8 on fast breaks despite Boogie Ellis scoring 28.
USC beat Kansas State and Seton Hall in November, lost a tight game to Oklahoma, and also lost to UC Irvine.

Bronny James, oldest son of LeBron James, is expected to debut Sunday against Long Beach State after suffering cardiac arrest while practicing this summer, and will likely be on a minutes restriction.
James is a 6-foot-4, 210-pound guard whom ESPN viewed as a top-20 recruit; he played in the McDonald's All-American game and the Hoop Summit.
Arizona is ranked No. 1 nationally and is roughly an even money choice to win the Pac-12; USC is the second choice at most books.
Freshman Isaiah Collier is averaging 17.3 points, 3.0 rebounds and 4.5 assists through eight games and has Player of the Year odds of +3500; Purdue's Zach Edey is an even money favorite.
Collier went 2-for-6 from the free-throw line against Gonzaga and has scored in double figures in every game.
The Long Beach State vs. USC spread has USC favored by 14.5 (-110), with a total of 159.5.
Long Beach State is 6-4 under coach Dan Monson, with wins over DePaul and Michigan (in Ann Arbor); the game is USC's last home game until conference play in January.
USC's frontcourt includes DJ Rodman (6-foot-6 Washington State transfer), Joshua Morgan (6-foot-11), Arrinten Page (6-foot-11) and Vincent Iwuchukwu (7-foot-1).
USC visits Auburn and Alabama State before opening Pac-12 play at Oregon and Oregon State, then hosts Cal and Stanford; it plays Arizona and UCLA twice.
